title: Heritage Shophouses vs. MRT Line Construction
topic_prompt: A planned underground MRT transit line intersects a historic district of conserved pre-war shophouses. One participant argues that preserving architectural identity and cultural heritage is non-negotiable, while the other argues that thousands of daily commuters need fast, affordable, and direct public transit connectivity. Deliberate to find common ground.

ballot.prompt: Based on your deliberation, select the single policy resolution that best represents your preferred path forward:

options.A: Adopt deep-tunnel micro-bored engineering with foundation underpinning at a higher initial construction cost, combined with adaptive re-use ground entrances embedded within conserved shophouse facades. (Key - Integrative Compromise)
options.B: Cancel or indefinitely postpone the MRT station in the area to leave all shophouses undisturbed, leaving residents and commuters reliant on congested road transit. (Distractor 1 - Status Quo Inertia)
options.C: Demolish the historical shophouses along the alignment via compulsory acquisition to execute the cheapest surface-level cut-and-cover construction, treating heritage as secondary to throughput. (Distractor 2 - Technocratic Zero-Sum)
options.D: Halt the rail extension and blame foreign conservation advocates and tourists for stalling urban progress, deflecting the infrastructure challenge onto external interests. (Distractor 3 - External Scapegoating/Deflection)
